outline: 1013 Angles in a Right Angle and Straight Line

examples.solution_text:
The marked angles are corresponding angles on parallel lines, so they are equal.

$x=55^{\circ}$

The marked angles lie between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal. They are alternate angles, so they are equal.

$y=125^{\circ}$

The marked angles are co-interior angles between parallel lines, so they sum to $180^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}z+125^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\z&=180^{\circ}-125^{\circ}\\z&=55^{\circ}\end{align*}$
The corresponding angles are equal: both measure $55^{\circ}$. Therefore $\ell$ and $m$ are parallel.

examples.derivation: The two marked sectors occupy corresponding positions. Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so x = 55°. The transversal coordinates give an inclination of 55°, consistent with both arcs. Supported by image268 and lines 2281–2286.

The upper sector spans 360° − 235° = 125°; the lower sector spans 180° − 55° = 125°. They are interior sectors on opposite sides of the transversal, so alternate-angle equality gives y = 125°. Supported by image286 and lines 2427–2432.
The marked sectors are interior angles on the same side of the transversal. Thus z + 125° = 180°, giving z = 55°. Both arc spans agree with these measures. Supported by image269 and lines 2281–2288.
Both marked angles occupy corresponding positions and measure 55°. Equal corresponding angles establish that ℓ and m are parallel without parallel markings. Supported by image281 and lines 2382–2390.
